newsitem.title: UK: N.Irish police find big home-made explosive cache.
newsitem.headline: N.Irish police find big home-made explosive cache.

text.p: Police found a large amount of home-made explosive in a search of a Roman Catholic housing estate in Londonderry, Northern Ireland's second city, on Sunday, security sources said.
They said three containers were found at the rear of a house, close to a coal bunker, and examined by army bomb disposal experts.
Houses were evacuated during the operation, which began on Sunday afternoon, residents said.
No official comment on the find was immediately available but police were expected to make an announcement on Sunday night, the sources said.
Home-made explosives are a favoured weapon of the Irish Republican Army (IRA), which is fighting British rule of Northern Ireland.
Londonderry is a stronghold of Catholic Irish nationalists from which the IRA has drawn support in its 28-year guerrilla war against Britain.
The find followed a week of tension between pro-British Loyalists and Catholic nationalists over the annual Protestant marching season.
Widespread Catholic rioting erupted one week ago after a Protestant Orange Order parade was routed through the nationalist Garvaghy Road zone of Portadown, south of Belfast.
The Orange Order scrapped four other parades after threats of mass Catholic counter-demonstrations but staged hundreds more on Saturday, the high point in its annual marching season.
The IRA ambushed a joint police and army security patrol in Belfast on Friday night, injuring five people.

Two teenaged Protestants were also shot and wounded on the same evening as they attended a bonfire party on the eve of the Orange Order's "Glorious 12th" celebrations marking a Protestant battle victory over a Catholic king in 1690.
